root_cause.text: The AMDGPU PCI probe code incorrectly made the global `amdgpu_aspm` setting depend on `pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)`, so on multi-GPU systems one AMD device could disable ASPM handling for another device that actually supported it, causing crashes due to the per-device ASPM refactor being bypassed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)) amdgpu_aspm = 0;` from `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/amdgpu/amdgpu_drv.c`, and the CVE text states this check was “erroneously applied again after commit 0ab5d711ec74 (‘drm/amd: Refactor `amdgpu_aspm` to be evaluated per device’)” and caused crashes on systems “with two AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove automatic ASPM disabling in the AMDGPU PCI probe path so the driver no longer overrides the configured ASPM state.
intent_record.what: The conditional block that checked `amdgpu_aspm == -1` and disabled `amdgpu_aspm` when `pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)` was false was removed from `amdgpu_pci_probe()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe path no longer automatically forces `amdgpu_aspm` to 0 based on PCIe ASPM being disabled, so the driver preserves the existing ASPM setting instead of overriding it during device initialization.

grouping_result.intent: Remove automatic ASPM disabling in the AMDGPU PCI probe path so the driver no longer overrides the configured ASPM state.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the AMDGPU probe-time logic that tied global ASPM behavior to a per-device PCIe check, preventing one GPU from disabling ASPM handling for others.

candidates.rationale: This condition makes the global amdgpu_aspm setting depend on the ASPM capability/state of the current PCI device, which can incorrectly disable ASPM handling for other GPUs on multi-GPU systems.
This assignment forcefully disables the global ASPM configuration when one device reports ASPM disabled, which is the direct misbehavior causing the per-device ASPM refactor to be bypassed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition ties the global amdgpu_aspm setting to the ASPM state of the current PCI device, so probing one GPU can disable ASPM handling for all AMD GPUs on a multi-GPU system, bypassing the per-device ASPM logic.
This assignment globally disables ASPM when a single device reports ASPM disabled, which is the incorrect behavior that caused the per-device ASPM refactor to be bypassed and led to crashes.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the new ASPM gating logic: `if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)) amdgpu_aspm = 0;`. This is the fix described in the commit message, because it checks whether the PCIe subsystem has ASPM enabled before leaving the global `amdgpu_aspm` default enabled. The vulnerable construct from the root cause—incorrectly making the global `amdgpu_aspm` depend on a per-device probe outcome in a way that could disable ASPM handling for other devices—is not present here as a bug; instead, the code explicitly disables AMDGPU ASPM only when PCIe ASPM is disabled by the subsystem. So the function already contains the fix and does not contain the vulnerable behavior.
